title: Member Orientation
description: New members are invited to join membership staff in the multipurpose room at Calder Gardens for a discussion about membership and how to access your benefits, followed by a contemplative walk through Calder Gardens. Explore the gardens and galleries in a small group, engaging in reflective close looking and conversations that inspire new and transformative perspectives on art and wellness.

title: Walks at Calder Gardens
description: Walks at Calder Gardens are intimate experiences designed to foster personal connections with art. Alongside specially trained guides, you will explore the gardens and galleries in small groups, engaging in reflective close-looking and conversations that inspire new and transformative perspectives on art and wellness. These 45-minute experiences are perfect for both new visitors and returning ones seeking a deeper exploration of how Alexander Calder's art, united with architecture and nature, offers different ways of thinking and feeling. Private walks are also available. Call 215.278.7250 for more information. Each walk is limited to 10 visitors.

title: Sound Passage by Gryphon Rue
description: Artist and composer Gryphon Rue presents a layered sonic installation that braids field recordings, wildlife, voice, and electronic sound into a fugue-like cycle of place, memory, and transformation. The composition turns continuously, without beginning or end, allowing sounds to surface, dissolve, overlap, and recur as a single unfolding organism. Source material includes: 'Glade' (musical saws, humpback whales recorded in Polynesia), 'Magenta Beams' (electronics, trumpets), Josephine Baker (collage), Auroral chorus (Sheffield, England; recordist: Mark Dennison), Spring peepers (High Falls, New York), Water well (Les Gras, France), 'Squatters Quarters' (percussion, tape manipulation), Echolocation of Indiana bats (North Georgia Mountains; recordist: Richard Devine), Electronic 'birds', Propane tank (High Falls, New York), 'Operation for Preferred Embodiment' (voice transformation).

title: Summer Listening Circle
description: Listening Circles, inspired by Indigenous talking circles, invite participants into a space of reflection, dialogue, and deep listening. Guided by Denise Dunkley, master artisan, educator, and member of the Nanticoke Lenni-Lenape Tribal Nation, each gathering creates opportunities for intergenerational exchange and shared learning through stories, lived experiences, and collective conversation. For the summer session, Dunkley will be joined by Sebastian Medina-Tayac (Piscataway Indian Nation), an Indigenous food sovereignty advocate, farmer, and educator who runs Red Cedar Farms in southern Maryland. His work centers on ancestral agricultural knowledge and Indigenous relationships to land, food, and community. For many Indigenous Peoples of the Amazon rainforest, círculos de la palabra—circles of the spoken word or talking circles—are essential communal gatherings where knowledge, memory, and care are shared.
location: Calder Gardens Disc (outdoor area near main entrance)
fee: Free; capacity is limited, and registration is encouraged

title: Silent Day at Calder Gardens
description: Join us for Silent Days at Calder Gardens, a program that invites visitors to slow down, turn inward, and experience quiet attention. Taking place each month, Silent Days offers after-hours access to the galleries and gardens dedicated to silence and sensory awareness with a reduced-audience capacity. We invite participants to experience silence as an enriching opportunity to engage with the world in an intentional and attentive way—an open field for noticing, listening, and being present. Designated areas for reading, drawing, writing, and meditation will be available throughout the galleries and gardens, with chairs, tables, and meditation cushions provided. Visitors are also welcome to bring their own meditation pillows for comfort. Conceived as a place for contemplation, Calder Gardens encourages visitors to learn more about themselves through direct, real-time experience. The works of Alexander Calder invite awareness through movement, balance, and experimentation; Herzog & de Meuron's building unfolds as a carefully choreographed sequence of sensorial moments; and Piet Oudolf's gardens draw attention to cycles of growth, decay, and transformation—reminding us of life's continual change. The reduced-sensory environment of Silent Days supports visitors with autism; social, emotional, or mental health needs; dementia, and other sensory sensitivities, while offering a more grounded and spacious experience for anyone seeking respite from the pace of daily life.

title: Member Walk
description: Members are invited to this members-only walk, offered during our member hour. Join us for a reflective journey through the different indoor and outdoor areas of Calder Gardens. You will be encouraged to slow down, notice your surroundings, and engage with the space in conversation, both with your guide and with one another.
